answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the summit schedule in the voyage ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the river checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 215 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. That is 10 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
